text:
Toronto arrives at Seattle with a four-game winning streak snapped, a 5-2 loss at Calgary two days ago, though they're still 4-1-0 in their last five. They're missing John Tavares (lower body), and in the five games since he went out Nick Paul has moved beside Nylander and McKenna. Seattle is coming off a 5-1 home loss to Minnesota four days ago and is 2-2-1 in its last five. They're without Jared McCann; Jordan Eberle has taken his spot and Matty Beniers is on the first power-play unit. The wrinkle: Bobby McMann faces the Maple Leafs for the first time since leaving them, after 200 games in their colours.

Neither team creates much. At five on five, Toronto has taken 45% of the expected goals (the quality of chances) and Seattle 44%, and both have results ahead of their chances. Toronto takes 4.5 penalties a game, which keeps handing out power plays. In net, projected starters Sergei Bobrovsky (+3.6 goals saved above expected this season, -13.5 last year) and Philipp Grubauer (+3.2 this season, +5.4 last) have both been solid early.

For Toronto, William Nylander is on a five-game point streak, and we have him at a 38% chance to score. Easton Cowan has 10 points in 10 games. For Seattle, Berkly Catton has nine in 10, and Eberle (29% to score) leads our numbers. Our under-the-radar pick is Shane Wright: he plays about 13:35 a night, but 2.7 expected goals in his last 10 games puts him ahead of 92% of depth forwards. We have him at 18% to score.
